title: 30 minute & Overnight Staining Flurophore Signature Comparisons
text:
In order to asses whether overnight staining requires overnight stained single color controls for accurate unmixing, something we suspected might be true due to consistent umixing error visible for some markers such as CD8, we compared the spectral signatures of our 2 sets of SC controls.
This was done by subtracting autofluorescence from the SC control, and then using a program written by David to graph the normalized fluorescence intensity of the fluorophore across all 54 detectors of the Aurora-4.
Here are the spectra of BV510-CD8 single color controls stained for 30 minutes and overnight, overlayed:

While they look very similar, here is a comparison of unmixing the same data (from the overnight stain of the D14 sample), where the only difference is the SC control provided for CD8



30 minute





Overnight


Clearly, even this small difference in fluorescent signature between SC controls is enough to change unmixing enough that it is visible.
For comparison, here are the overlayed signatures for BUV496-CD4, which had not previously shown any sign of unmixing error.

These two signatures are so similar, despite their different staining times, that they appear as one line. In the future, investigation of what fluorophores change during overnight staining could be useful.

title: 30 minute & Overnight Staining of Sigle Color Controls on Enriched T cells
text:
Protocol
Single color controls were prepared on enriched T cells for the 30 color panel. Samples were stained according to the following table, leaving out the PE and CD19 stains as there would be no positive population in the enriched T cells.


10 million enriched T cells suspended in approximatly 1 mL of PBS were obtained from David Yamoah for staining.
Cells were incubated with 5 uL of TruStain FcX for 15 minutes in the fridge.
Sample was diluted to 8.5 mL of volume and vortexed to ensure even distribution.
56 5 mL FACS tubes were obtained and labled with the 27 flurophores & markers to be stained. 2 tubes were designated for unstained samples.

One set of tubes labled with the 27 fluorophores was to be stained at the higher antibody stain concentration listed in the table for 30 minutes, to act as SC controls for the previously optimized sequentially stained panel.
The other set was to be stained at the lower concentration listed in the table overnight, to act as SC controls for the new overnight staining protocol.

150 uL of the enriched T cell solution was aliquoted into each tube, so that each would contain roughly 150k cells.
Appropriate amounts of antibody were aliqouted into the labled tubes, according to the table above. Samples were vortexed after addition of antibody and placed in the fridge for their incubation times.
After incubation, 1 mL of PBS was added to each sample tube, and samples were centrifuged at 300xg for 5 minutes to wash away any unbound antibody.
Supernatent was discarded, and samples were resuspended in 100 uL of PBS.
Samples were analyzed with the Aurora-4 spectral cytometer.

title: Result of Testing Fixation for Overnight Staining of PBMCs
text:
Wash of Overnight Stained Samples
1 mL of PBS was added to all samples, which were then centrifuged at 300 xg for 5 minutes. Supernatent was discarded and samples were resuspended in 180 uL of PBS. The fixed and unfixed unstained samples were divided into 2 tubes each, of which one of the 2 would have 7-AAD added, and the other would serve as a true unstained sample for fixed and unfixed cells.
5 uL of 7-AAD viability dye was added to the fixed & unfixed overnight backbone stains, as well as the designated fixed & unfixed unstained samples. These were placed in the fridge to incubate for 5 minutes.


Compensation/Unmixing Issues
Fixed & Unfixed backbone stains were both unmixed with unfixed single color controls. After unmixing, there appeared to be some unmixing error especially for the CD4/CD8 markers. David & discussed several possible reasons for this. Since the PBMC samples were cryopresrved & thawed quickly, they could have been damaged in a way that impacted autofluoresence, and caused more than one AF signature. It is also possible that the fixed backbone stain needs to be unmixed with single color controls that have also been fixed, since fixation is known to somewhat alter the Af signature of cells.

Backbone and Full Panel stains run overnight were not incubated with 7-AAD viability dye before analysis.

After incubation, these samples were washed with 1 mL of running buffer and centrifuged at 300 xg for 5 minutes, then resuspended in 180 uL of running buffer. 5 uL of 7-AAD was then added to both samples; they were incubated for 5 minutes before analysis.


Full Panel

Backbone


The 30 min backbone stain had a small CAR positive population, however the overnight backbone stain only had about 2% CAR positive, suggesting that using the CAR detection reagent before the rest of the antibodies is not effective for good resolution of CAR populations in overnight staining.

title: CAR T Cell Full Panel and Backbone Stain Attempt 2
text:
Full Panel
There was a clear population of CD3 positive lymphocytes present in this population, and a sufficient number of cells to collect over 100k events. However, there was not a large or particularly clear population positive for the CAR marker.
It is possible that there inclusion of so many markers negatively impacted the staining and resolution of the CAR T detection reagent. There are several potential future experiments that could be run to assess this.
The next step planned is to stain CAR T cells with the CAR detection reagent overnight alongside the rest of the antibody cocktail, instead of staining seperately and washing off the CAR detection reagent before staining with the antibody cocktail.

title: CAR T Cell Full Panel and Backbone Stain Attempt 2
text:
Backbone
A smaller number of cells was available, with fewer CD3 positve cells compared to the sample stained with the full panel, however there was still a population of CD3 positive lymphocytes. Unlike the full panel, a resolvable population positive for the CAR detection marker was present. This supports the idea that the presense of so many antibodies in the full panel may be impacting the resolution of the CAR detection.

RR668 and Biotin-PE inclusion did not seem to negatively impact resolution of the backbone antibodies, as seen in comparison of populations in the full backbone stained sample, and the sample that did not include RR688 and PE. However, there were far fewer cells in the full backbone stain, so this is difficult to see.

In future experiments, it seems as though RR688 and Biotin-PE should be included in the backbone cocktail.

title: Results of 30-Minute Full Panel & Backbone Stains
text:
Result of 30 Minute Backbone Stain of Enriched T cells
The enriched T cells that were incubated for 30 minutes in the backbone antibody stain cocktail were analyzed with the Aurora 4 spectral cytometer. Antibodies in the backbone cocktail were included based on the fact that they typically stain well and provide good resolution between positive and negative populations with standard staining and sequential staining. Therefore, it was predicted that populations would be easy to resolve for all markers in this stain. This prediction proved correct, as can be seen by the figures below.
Unmixing was done using previously collected single stain contols (of cells or beads), and the unstained sample collected from the same batch of thawed enriched T cells as was stained.



Result of 30 Minute Full Panel Stain of Enriched T Cells
The enriched T cells that were incubated for 30 minutes in the full panel (27 color) cocktail of antibodies were also analyzed with the Aurora 4 spectral cytometer. This panel had previously been run with a sequential staining protocol, wherein some antibody stains were added to the cell same earlier than others, based on reduced marker binding affinity or rarity of the marker. Somewhat surprisingly, most markers did still show resolution of positive and negative populations, although some were more clearly defined than others.

Overnight Single Color Controls at Low Concentration
text:
In order to optimize the panel for overnight staining, it is nessecery to determine the appropriate antibody titrations to be used. Since the overnight stain involves much longer incubation time, it is likely that the original antibody quantities used will cause staining that is too bright or contribute to non-specific staining.
Single color controls could also be used to unmix the full cocktail sample that was incubated overnight at these lower concentrations.

title: Results of Overnight CART Stain (Full and Backbone)
text: About 80% of cells appeared to be alive after overnight incubation in fridge, this was determined with 7-AAD viability dye. Markers included in the backbone stained well enough to allow for populations to be resolved, however, as anticipated based on analysis of the cells used with the MACSQuant, the CAR reagent & biotin markers (RR688 & PE fluorophores) did not show positive populations.

title: Results of Overnight CART Stain (Full and Backbone)
text:
Full Panel (No Medium)
No significant positive population was observed for CAR marker after gating on healthy, live, CD3 positive cells.

title: Results of Overnight CART Stain (Full and Backbone)
text:
Full Panel (Medium)
The inclusion of medium did increase the proportion of viable cells following overnight incubation as compared with the sample incubated in only running buffer. It appears that the inclusion of medium did impact antibody binding, and reduced resolution was observed for several markers when compared to the sample without medium.
It was determined that in future experiments, medium is likely not a useful way to account for cell death during the long incubation, due to the impact on antibody binding and population resolution. Possible next steps include the use of different medium, or fixing cells prior to staining.

title: Testing PFA for Overnight Staining of PBMCs
text:
Background
Dr. Fan, Rediet, and myself, have previously noticed and been concened by the proportion of cells that appear to die over the course of overnight incubation. Previously, one way that we have sought to increase the proportional of cells that remain viable is to incubate cells overnight in a complete medium, as opposed to PBS. This did improve the number of cells which survived overnight incubation, but had a detrimental effect on the resolution of many markers, and thus was deemed to be a poor solution.
Based on the protocols reccomended in the paper “Improving High Parameter Cytometry with Overnight Staining”, I decided to test fixation of the samples to be stained overnight.


Protocol
PBMCs that had been cyropreseved by David Rach were thawed, they were suspended in R10 (10% FBS, 1% L-glutamine, and 0.1% gentamycin) for cryopresevation. 2 mL of sample, containing 6 million samples, were retrieved. 650 uL of sample was aliquoted into 3 5-mL FACS tubes (2M cells per tube).
2 mL of PBS was added to each sample tube and samples were centrifuged at 300 xg for 5 minutes to wash away R10 solution. Supernatent was discarded and samples were resuspended in 100 uL of PBS. The sample that would be used for single-color stains was resuspended in 600 uL PBS (100 uL per antibody that would be part of the single stain).
5 uL of TruStain FcX was added to each sample, and samples were allowed to incubate in the fridge for at least 5 minutes.
While samples were incubating, 4% PFA fixative was obtained and diluted to 0.4% (10 uL of PFA and 90 uL of PBS were added to an eppendorf tube and mixed well).
After incubation with FcX, each tube (containing 100 uL of cell solution) was split into 2 50 uL aliquots. These 4 samples were labled “unstained, unstained-fixed, backbone, backbone-fixed”. 50 uL of the 0.4% PFA solution was added to the two samples labled for fixation, and these samples were incubated in the fridge for 20 minutes.
100 uL of the single-color sample was aliqoted into each of 6 tubes, labled with the antibody-fluorophore conjugate that would be added to that tube.
Backbone cocktail was prepared, containing the following:

title: Testing Fixation & Overnight Fixation on CAR T cells
text:
Protocol
CAR T cell sample was obtained by Rediet Mulatu from patient at APH and D14 time points. 5 uL of TruStain FcX was added to each sample, and samples were allowed to incubate in the fridge for at least 5 minutes.
While samples were incubated with FcX, the antibody cocktail was prepared according to the following table:

Cells were aliquoted into unstained, backbone, and full stain samples for both the APH and D14 samples. Antibody cocktail was added to the appropriate samples.
After overnight incubation, 1 mL of PBS was added to samples, which were then centrifuged at 300xg for 5 minutes. Supernatent was discarded and samples were resuspended in 180 uL of PBS.
Backbone and full stain samples for both time points were then incubated for 15 minutes with 2 uL of CAR detection reagent, washed, and then stained with 1 uL of PE-biotin for CAR detection.
Samples were then washed once again, by centrifugation at 300xg for 5 mins. Supernatent was discarded and samples were once again resuspended in 180 uL of PBS.
5uL of 7-AAD viability dye was added to backbone and full stains, and allowed to incubate for 5 minutes in the fridge.
Samples were then anaylzed on the Aurora-4, and unmixed using the overnight SC controls collected on this day (7/28).

title: Result of Overnight Staining Protocol CAR T cells
text:
The protocol we have decided to use for staining of CAR T clinical samples appears promising, and was presented using this flow chart:

Since there was an APH as well as a D14 sample stained this time, we were able to confirm that our protocol does not result in excessive non-specific staining of the CAR detection marker. This is shown below, by the fact that our CAR + populatoon is only visible in the D14 sample from this patient.


We also saw clear resolutions for populations positive and negative for CD319, an activation marker known to be hard to resolve in high-parameter panels
